channel.title: Learn Hangul – ggook's studio
channel.description: Free guides to the Korean alphabet, from your first letter to reading real words.

item.title: Ordering at a Korean Restaurant: Phrases From Door to Bill
item.description: Everything you need to eat out in Korea: how many people, calling the server, ordering and asking for more side dishes, spice levels, takeout and paying at the counter.

item.title: Days, Weeks and Dates in Korean
item.description: The days of the week and the elements behind their names, yesterday to the day after tomorrow, parts of the day, and how to ask and say the date.

item.title: 은/는 or 이/가? Korean Topic and Subject Particles Explained
item.description: The two particles every Korean learner mixes up. Learn which form to use, the core difference between topic and subject, and seven situations that show when to choose each.

item.title: Everyday Korean Greetings and Phrases for Real Situations
item.description: Hello, goodbye, thank you and sorry, plus the phrases Koreans say at meals, at work, in shops and on holidays, with what each one literally means.

item.title: Korean Family Terms: 형, 오빠, 누나, 언니 and Beyond
item.description: Why there are four words for an older sibling, how Koreans name relatives on each side of the family, and why you'll hear 언니 and 이모 used for people who aren't family at all.

item.title: Korean Politeness Basics: -요, -습니다 and Casual Speech
item.description: Korean sentences end differently depending on who you're talking to. Learn the three speech styles you'll actually use, how to make the -요 form, and when it's OK to speak casually.

item.title: Korean Numbers: Native and Sino-Korean, and When to Use Each
item.description: Korean has two sets of numbers. Learn both, the rule of thumb for choosing between them, and the everyday cases: time, money, dates, age and counting things.

item.title: A Two-Week Plan to Learn Hangul
item.description: Fifteen to twenty minutes a day for two weeks: a day-by-day plan that takes you from your first letter to reading signs and menus.

item.title: Batchim: Final Consonants and the Seven End Sounds
item.description: Why 옷, 낮 and 꽃 all end the same way, how final consonants move to the next syllable, and the few sound changes every beginner should know.

item.title: Plain, Aspirated and Tense: Hearing ㄱ, ㅋ and ㄲ
item.description: Korean has three kinds of g/k, d/t, b/p and j/ch sounds. Learn what makes them different, with word sets to listen to and a simple tissue test.

item.title: Korean Vowels: From ㅏ to ㅢ
item.description: The 10 basic vowels, the 11 compound vowels built from them, and which ones sound the same in everyday Korean today.

item.title: Korean Consonants: All 14 Basic Letters, With Sounds
item.description: Every basic Korean consonant with its name, its sound at the start and end of a syllable, and an example word you can listen to.

item.title: How Hangul Works: The Korean Alphabet Explained
item.description: Where Hangul came from, the 24 basic letters, and how letters stack into syllable blocks. Start here if you've never read Korean.
